subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Balance: 2H2 + O2 -> ?H2O. What number goes in front of H2O?
questions.explain: 2H2O gives 4 H and 2 O, balancing 2H2 (4 H) and O2 (2 O).

questions.q: What is the formula of the compound formed from Mg²⁺ and Cl⁻ ions?
questions.explain: Two Cl⁻ ions balance one Mg²⁺ ion, giving MgCl2.

questions.q: Why is a high atom economy desirable in industry?
options: It produces less waste and uses resources efficiently
questions.explain: High atom economy means more reactant atoms end up in the useful product, reducing waste.

questions.q: Balance: N2 + ?H2 → 2NH3. What number goes in front of H2?
questions.explain: 3H2 gives 6 H atoms, matching 2NH3 (6 H), and N2 gives 2 N.

questions.q: A reaction has a theoretical yield of 50 g but only 40 g is obtained. What is the percentage yield?
What is the mass of 3 mol of carbon atoms? (Ar = 12)
questions.explain: mass = moles x Ar = 3 x 12 = 36 g.

questions.q: What is the Mr of carbon dioxide, CO2? (Ar: C=12, O=16)
What is the concentration in mol/dm3 of 0.1 mol of solute dissolved in 0.5 dm3?
What is the mass of 0.5 mol of CaCO3? (Mr = 100)
How many moles are in 100 g of calcium carbonate, CaCO3? (Mr = 100)
Atom economy is a measure of:
options: The proportion of reactant atoms that become the desired product
questions.explain: Atom economy measures how much of the reactants' mass ends up as useful product.

questions.q: What is the formula of the ionic compound aluminium oxide, from Al³⁺ and O²⁻?
When magnesium burns, the mass appears to increase. Why?
options: Oxygen from the air combines with the magnesium
The magnesium gives off a gas
questions.explain: Oxygen from the air joins the magnesium to form magnesium oxide, so the solid mass increases.

questions.q: What is the Mr of magnesium oxide, MgO? (Ar: Mg=24, O=16)
In a closed system, the total mass of the products of a reaction is:
questions.explain: Mass is conserved, so the products have the same total mass as the reactants.

questions.q: A compound contains 0.3 mol of nitrogen and 0.9 mol of hydrogen. What is its empirical formula?
questions.explain: The ratio 0.3:0.9 simplifies to 1:3, giving NH3.

questions.q: A compound contains 0.2 mol carbon and 0.4 mol hydrogen. What is its empirical formula?
questions.explain: The ratio 0.2:0.4 simplifies to 1:2, giving CH2.

questions.q: What is the Mr of sodium hydroxide, NaOH? (Ar: Na=23, O=16, H=1)
What is the concentration in mol/dm³ of a solution with 0.5 mol of solute in 2 dm³?
A solution has a concentration of 25 g/dm3. What mass of solute is in 2 dm3?
questions.explain: mass = concentration x volume = 25 x 2 = 50 g.

questions.q: Approximately how many particles are in one mole of a substance (Avogadro's constant)?
How many moles are in 36 g of water, H2O? (Mr = 18)
